# SwogeAgentic

> Pay-per-call tools for AI agents from SWOGE WORLD: token scans (market from DexScreener, contract security Powered by Go+ Security, and what the SWOGE AI colony measured on Robinhood Chain, with sample sizes), the colony's newest launches and live activity, wallet and infrastructure OSINT (passive), the $SWOGE economy, web search, image generation and a full research agent. Read-only: nothing here buys, sells or signs. Each call is paid from the key owner's $SWOGE balance, within a daily cap they set.

Get an API key at https://swoleeswoge.dog/swogeagentic.html (sign in with a wallet, set a daily cap; the key is shown once). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer swg_…`.

REST: `GET https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/agentic/tools` lists tools, prices and input schemas. `POST https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/agentic/call/<tool>` with `{"arguments": {...}}` runs one; add `"quote": true` to get the price without paying — no key needed for a quote. Every paid call returns `facture` (the exact amount billed, as a string), `recu` (a receipt id) and `solde` (the balance left). Refused calls (bad input, tool failure, cap reached) are never billed. Errors: 400 bad input, 401 no key (the answer says how to pay) or revoked key, 402 balance or daily cap, 404 unknown tool, 429 over 60 calls/minute/key, 502 tool failed, 503 unavailable.

No account? Pay per call with x402 (v2): call `POST https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/agentic/call/<tool>` without a key and read the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header (402) — scheme `exact`, network `eip155:4663`, paid in USDG `0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168` (eip3009) or SWOGE `0x8a166Fb41Cd659a0a43396272FF73973Ce29F817` (permit2). Sign and retry with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`; we pay the gas. Price: tool price + settlement gas, minimum $0.02. Fixed-price tools, and `generate_image` at a fixed price per request (the 402 quotes that exact request: pay it with the same arguments). `ask_agent` and `generate_video` need an API key. With $SWOGE and no Permit2 allowance yet, add the `eip2612GasSponsoring` extension (permit value = the exact amount). Status: `GET https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/agentic/x402`.

MCP: Streamable HTTP at `https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/mcp` with the same bearer key — `tools/list` and `quote: true` work without one (protocol 2026-07-28, and 2025-11-25 / 2025-06-18 / 2025-03-26 via initialize). Every tool also takes `quote: true`. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http swogeagentic https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer swg_…"`.

Tools:

- `scan_token(address)` — $0.01. Use this before buying, listing or writing about an EVM token, to check its market and its contract in one call (contract security Powered by Go+ Security, https://gopluslabs.io).
- `can_i_sell(address)` — $0.008. Use this right before buying a Robinhood Chain token, to know whether you could sell it back and at what cost.
- `colony_activity(token?)` — $0.005. Use this when you want to know what the SWOGE AI colony, an autonomous paper-trading colony on Robinhood Chain, holds or did recently, overall or on one token.
- `swoge_economy()` — $0.001. Use this when you need the current state of the $SWOGE token economy.
- `new_launches(limit?)` — $0.005. Use this when you want the newest tokens on Robinhood Chain, minutes after their pool opens, with what an autonomous trading colony decided about each.
- `wallet_intel(address)` — $0.008. Use this when you need to know who is behind an EVM address, typically a token deployer, before trusting what it launches.
- `osint_lookup(target)` — $0.008. Use this when you need passive reconnaissance on internet infrastructure: a domain, an IP address, a website URL, an autonomous system (AS15169) or a CVE id.
- `web_search(query)` — $0.0075. Use this when the answer is outside SWOGE data: news, projects, teams, people, anything on the open web.
- `chat_completion(model?, messages, max_tokens?)` — real cost, up to $undefined. Use this when you need an answer from a frontier AI model without an account or an API key: Claude (Opus, Fable, Sonnet, Haiku), GPT-6 or Grok, one call.
- `robinhood_token(address)` — $0.003. Use this when you need to know what a Robinhood Chain contract is before touching it: one call, decoded.
- `robinhood_wallet(address, tokens?)` — $0.003. Use this when you need the holdings of a Robinhood Chain address: ETH plus up to 20 tokens, read on-chain in one Multicall3 call.
- `robinhood_tx(hash)` — $0.003. Use this when you need to understand what a Robinhood Chain transaction did.
- `robinhood_rpc(method, params?)` — $0.003. Use this when you need a raw read on Robinhood Chain (chain id 4663) without running a node: one read-only JSON-RPC call.
- `token_verdict(address)` — $0.008. Use this when you must decide fast whether an EVM token is worth a closer look: one verdict you can branch on (red_flags, caution, unknown or no_red_flag_found) with its reasons.
- `stock_token_check(address?, symbol?)` — $0.005. Use this before touching a stock token on Robinhood Chain (NVDA, TSLA, SPY…): it tells whether a contract is the official Robinhood Stock Token or a copy using the same ticker.
- `stock_tokens_premium(limit?, min_liquidity_usd?)` — $0.005. Use this when you want the Robinhood Chain stock tokens whose on-chain pools trade furthest from their Chainlink feed.
- `base_launches(platform?, limit?, traded_only?)` — $0.005. Use this when you want the newest memecoin launches on Base (Clanker v4 and Zora coins), read on-chain: each with its deployer and the deployer's MEASURED record.
- `base_deployer(address)` — $0.005. Use this when you need the track record of an address that launches tokens on Base (Clanker v4 or Zora).
- `fair_commit()` — $0.001. Use this before any draw other players must trust (a game between agents, a raffle, a giveaway): the server picks a secret seed and publishes its SHA-256 hash now, so it cannot change the seed later.
- `fair_draw(commitment_id, client_seed, count?, min?, max?)` — $0.001. Use this after fair_commit, once every player has seen the server_seed_hash: give your client_seed and get uniform random integers in [min, max].
- `fair_verify(server_seed, server_seed_hash?, client_seed, scheme?, count?, min?, max?, numbers?, nonce?)` — $0.001. Use this to check a draw independently: recomputes the SHA-256 of a revealed server_seed against its hash, and the numbers of a swoge-hmac-sha256-v1 draw, or the 52-card shoe of a SWOGE casino hand (scheme swoge-casino-shoe with its nonce).
- `roast_token(address)` — $0.015. Use this when you want a funny, shareable take on an EVM token for a post or a chat: SWOGE, a very muscular shiba inu, roasts it in 2 or 3 sentences built only on its real data.
- `ask_agent(task, model?)` — real cost, up to $1.296. Use this when a question needs several of these tools chained together and a written answer, for example comparing tokens or researching a launcher.
- `generate_image(prompt, provider?, quality?, aspect_ratio?, count?)` — real cost, up to $0.7037. Use this when you need an image: an illustration, a meme, a post visual, or the SWOGE character (a prompt that names SWOGE is drawn from the official character).
- `generate_video(prompt, quality?, duration?, resolution?, aspect_ratio?)` — real cost, up to $3.6. Use this when you need a short video clip, 6 or 10 seconds, made with Grok Imagine.
- `video_status(id)` — free. Use this when you started a video with generate_video and want to know whether it is ready.

Travel eSIM, no account: `GET https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/esim/plans?country=France` (free) lists data-only eSIM plans for a country or a region (Europe, Asia, Middle East, South America, North America, Global), cheapest per GB first, each with `priceUsd`. `POST https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/esim/buy` with `{"plan": "<plan id>"}` answers 402 (x402 v2, USDC on Base or Solana, the plan price); sign and retry with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` and the same plan. The eSIM is bought before the payment settles: if it cannot be bought, nothing is charged. The answer carries the activation (LPA code) and `orderLink`, a secret: `GET https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/esim/order/<orderLink>` returns it again. Data only, no phone number; check the device supports eSIM.

Pay other x402 services with your key: `POST https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/agentic/pay` with `{"url": "...", "query": {...}, "max_usd": 0.01}` and an `Idempotency-Key` header. The key owner turns payments on for that key first (per-call cap up to $0.10, optional allowed sites); SWOGE pays, only if the service answers 200, and bills the owner in $SWOGE. The same Idempotency-Key never pays twice. Every attempt is on a hash-chained audit: `GET https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/agentic/audit`.

## Docs

- [API documentation](https://swoleeswoge.dog/swogeagentic_api.html): authentication, endpoints, MCP setup, errors, examples
- [Live tool catalogue (JSON)](https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/agentic/tools): tools, prices in $ and $SWOGE, input schemas
- [OpenAPI 3.1](https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/openapi.json): every tool as an operation, with x-payment-info on those payable without a key
- [Live llms.txt](https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/llms.txt): this file, generated from the live catalogue
- [Travel eSIM plans (JSON, free)](https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/esim/plans?country=France): search, then buy with x402 at /esim/buy
- [x402 services measured by SWOGE (JSON, free)](https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/agentic/services?q=price): the public catalogue with probes, latency and real paid calls; no verdict under 3 probes
- [x402 discovery manifest](https://web-production-220a3.up.railway.app/.well-known/x402): the resources payable per call
